newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels advance, new recruits parade.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels advance, new recruits parade.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila on Thursday listed fresh advances by his forces and told some 5,000 newly-trained troops they had a duty to remove President Mobutu Sese Seko and his "corrupt and rotten system".

Dressed in new U.S.-type combat fatigues and wellington boots, the recruits sang battle songs praising Kabila and denouncing Mobutu as they marched through Goma watched by many of its 300,000 residents.
"You and I have a duty to remove Mobutu and his corrupt and rotten system and relegate them to the dustbins of history," Kabila said.

"This army we are building is the medicine to end the ills of Zaire, ills created by greed and moral bankruptcy. I now command you to go to the front and rescue your beautiful and rich country from the chains of slavery."

The rebel leader told Reuters that his forces had taken the eastern town of Shabunda on Wednesday and were now fighting in Isiro, about 520 km (325 miles) northwest of Goma, which fell to the rebels in early November.
He said some of the 300 mercenaries hired by Kinshasa to crush the eastern revolt - many of them from former Yugoslavia - were based in Isiro.
Kabila said rebels now controlled an area 1,400 km (875 miles) long.

Church sources and aid workers said earlier on Thursday that the rebels had captured Shabunda and were advancing towards Kindu, which has an army base and airport and was a springboard for a government army counter-offensive launched last month.
Commanders in Goma said rebel forces were now within reach of the town of Moba in the southeast.
"Our frontline units are within reach of Moba. The town is now within reach of our firepower and we detect no major difficulties in capturing it," a rebel commander told Reuters.
Rebels said Moba was a gateway to Zaire's copper and cobalt-rich Shaba province.
Kabila's radio station in Goma broadcast an appeal to King Hassan of Morocco not to provide military aid to Mobutu, who is visiting his longtime ally.
The Zairean leader is in Morocco on his way home from France where he has been convalescing from prostate cancer surgery.
Moroccan troops in 1977 helped put down a secessionist uprising in Shaba after Zairean forces failed to make headway.
The United States said on Wednesday it had urged Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi to stay out of the fighting in east Zaire.
Zaire has accused all three of sending their troops to fight alongside the rebels. All three countries, which border on rebel-held territory, deny doing so.
